# deceptive intent claim

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:deceptiveIntentClaim`](gmeow-deceptiveIntentClaim.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/deceptiveIntentClaim>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/deception`](../../slices/deception.md)
- **Box roles:** [CBox role](../boxes/cbox.md), [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

An attributed, defeasible standpoint claim that the event was carried out with deceptive intent. The vantage is the assessor (who attributes the intent), not the deceiver; the claim carries [`gmeow:confidence`](gmeow-confidence.md) and [`gmeow:wasAttributedTo`](gmeow-wasAttributedTo.md). Intent is NEVER entailed by the reasoner — it is a contestable attribution that coexists with its denial ([Principle 9](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-9)).

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to attach an assessor's attribution that an event was deliberately deceptive — keeping intent OUT of the logic, as a confidence-weighted, attributed claim rather than an entailed fact (the lie/error/bullshit distinction turns on intent the reasoner must not decide).

### Avoid when

- Avoid asserting intent as a global fact or boolean flag, and avoid putting the deceiver in the vantage — the vantage is the ASSESSOR; never let the reasoner entail deceptiveness (it is contestable and coexists with its denial, [Principle 9](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-9)).

### How to use

- Mint a [`gmeow:StandpointClaim`](../classes/gmeow-StandpointClaim.md) whose [`gmeow:vantage`](gmeow-vantage.md) is the assessor, carry [`gmeow:confidence`](gmeow-confidence.md) and [`gmeow:wasAttributedTo`](gmeow-wasAttributedTo.md), and link it via [`gmeow:deceptiveIntentClaim`](gmeow-deceptiveIntentClaim.md); record a denial as a separate coexisting claim rather than negating this one.

### Examples
